probes.name: PG1
probes.subject: tests/conftest.py
probes.note: 🔴 The s295 incident itself: the guard computes the names and strips none of them. The child's git fixtures then write into whatever GIT_DIR names — here the throwaway victim, in s295 the real repository.

probes.name: PG2
probes.subject: tests/conftest.py
probes.note: The same mutation on the non-vacuity control. Unguarded, the two driven nodes fail (measured s296: 27 failed across the seven git-writing files), so the child's own exit code reddens — which is what rules out 'the victim was untouched because the child never ran'.

probes.name: PG3
probes.subject: tests/conftest.py
probes.note: The absence assertion, witnessed where it can fail. Unguarded, the child's own environment still holds GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE, so the payload node reddens inside the child and the parent reads a non-zero code.

probes.name: PG4
probes.subject: tests/test_git_env_guard.py
probes.note: Instrument control (Lesson #0056). The snapshot goes blind to config, which is the field carrying the s295 identity rewrite. A blind instrument reports 'unchanged' on every run, so this has to be able to go RED before the byte-identical assertion means anything.

probes.name: PG5
probes.subject: tests/test_git_env_guard.py
probes.note: The same control for the other dimension. s295 created a branch as well as rewriting the identity, so one control per field — config blind and refs blind are different failures and neither covers the other.

probes.name: PG6
probes.subject: tests/conftest.py
probes.old: name.startswith("GIT_") and name not in keep
probes.new: name.startswith("ZZZ_") and name not in keep
probes.note: The sweep stops recognising its own prefix and returns nothing. Witnesses that the listed names are found because they are GIT_-prefixed, not by accident of ordering.

probes.name: PG7
probes.subject: tests/conftest.py
probes.old: name.startswith("GIT_") and name not in keep
probes.new: name.startswith("GIT") and name not in keep
probes.note: 🔴 The one-character slip that would break CI: drop the underscore and GITHUB_TOKEN / GITHUB_SHA become 'git variables' and get deleted from the environment of every CI run. The test that says GITHUB_ survives is an absence assertion, so it needs exactly this mutation to prove it is not vacuous.

probes.name: PG8
probes.subject: tests/conftest.py
probes.old: return sorted(name for name in env if name.startswith("GIT_") and name not in keep)
probes.new: return sorted(name for name in env if name.startswith("GIT_"))
probes.note: The keep-list stops being consulted. _GIT_ENV_KEEP is empty today, so nothing in the suite's own behaviour would change and no other test could notice — this probe is the only thing standing between the policy knob and silent decoration.

exemptions.test_this_process_has_no_inherited_git_v: Structurally unreachable by any mutation of the guard: run from a clean shell the parent process has no GIT_* to begin with, so the assertion holds whether or not the guard stripped anything. Registered rather than probed. Its content IS witnessed — PG3 runs this very node inside a child spawned with GIT_DIR and GIT_WORK_TREE set, where it reddens.
